facts.summary: The preliminary report describes the Panel as a standing UN scientific assessment mechanism designed for sustained, iterative work. Its role is to document evidence, consensus, disagreements and gaps while remaining policy-relevant but not policy-prescriptive.
facts.document_status: Preliminary scientific report, July 2026; institutional self-description at publication.

facts.quote:
Most countries, including 
many advanced economies, lack the technical expertise to assess the most capable
facts.summary: The report identifies uneven national capacity to assess frontier models and participate in their governance, with evaluation expertise, compute and language data concentrated where AI is developed.
facts.document_status: Preliminary scientific assessment, July 2026; capacity finding.

facts.quote: Access to AI tools alone does not produce equal benefit
facts.summary: Effective and safe AI deployment also depends on complementary investment in data, skills, workflows and institutions; the Panel presents its preliminary evidence base as one contribution to building Member State capacity.
facts.document_status: Preliminary scientific assessment, July 2026; not a funding commitment.

facts.summary: The report cites developer-defined risk thresholds and fragmented regional governance as reasons for independent scientific assessment and shared evidence standards.
facts.document_status: Preliminary scientific assessment, July 2026; diagnosis rather than an adopted governance rule.

facts.summary: The report primarily addresses broadly capable foundation and general-purpose models deployed at scale, while distinguishing narrower systems whose usefulness depends on defined tasks, available data and institutional deployment capacity.
facts.document_status: Preliminary scientific report, July 2026; stated analytical scope.
